headline: Price has won 14 of 17 meetings with Van Veen before final
standfirst: Gerwyn Price, a former champion, meets Gian van Veen, still without a title in 12 months, in tonight's Grand Slam of Darts final. Throws start at 7:45pm.
body: The head-to-head is lopsided. Gerwyn Price has beaten Gian van Veen 14 times in 17 meetings, and the pair meet in the Grand Slam of Darts final at 7:45pm in a first-to-16 match. The runner-up takes home £100,000.

Price, ranked fourth, is a former winner of this event, having lifted the trophy in 2018. He has four titles in the last 12 months and an average of 98.66 across 138 matches, 95 of them won. That is more than three points above his opponent over the same period.

Van Veen is ranked third but has not won a title in the last 12 months. His average over that time is 95.27, from 99 wins in 163 matches. His previous best at this tournament was a quarter-final in 2024, so he is already in uncharted territory in Wolverhampton.

Both come in on a run of wins. Price edged Niko Springer 16-15 in an earlier round and then beat Ryan Searle 10-7 before the quarter-finals. Van Veen beat Nathan Aspinall 16-14 and Martin Schindler 10-7 on the way.

Price is the clear favourite on history, but Van Veen is ranked a place higher and a first major title would be a breakthrough for a player who has reached finals day without one in the last 12 months.
